summary: Kin Cheung specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

King Chung Lo studied at Fudan University and completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig under Eli Franco. He held research positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig, the New Asia Institute, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Manchester under the supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva was a historian who studied at the University of London (~1959–1962). He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya from circa 1969 to 1995.

Kirby Flower Smith studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield, Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve, and Minton Warren. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and directed the American School of Classical Studies in Rome (1914–1915).

Kirill Solonin works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Fo Guang University (~2005–2013) and has been a professor at Renmin University of China since circa 2013.
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indologist who completed his studies at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kishor Chaudhari earned a master's in English from Kavayitri Bahinabai Chaudhari North Maharashtra University in 2013. Working in Indology and religious studies, he became an assistant professor at Government Science College, Chhota Udepur, in 2018.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under several traditional teachers—including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya and Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha—as well as Gopinath Bhattacharya and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Philosopher Kitaro Nishida studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz and earned a doctorate from Kyoto University. He taught at Fourth Higher School and Gakushuin before serving as professor of philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda completed doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973). Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1993) and director of the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).
Kiyoshi Kato studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Otani University (1927–1931) under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).

Kiyoshi Miki was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920). He held academic posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University (~1920–1922).

Kiyoshi Okano, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as an associate professor (attested 2002) and as professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe completed doctoral studies at Rissho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 2001). He was affiliated with the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra as a special researcher in 2001.

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi worked in Sinology and the history of archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929), where he later held an academic post (~1935–1969) before serving at Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Shitennoji University, the University of Tokyo, Tsurumi University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and served as president of Tsurumi Women's University.

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. A specialist in Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Toyo Bunko, Hokkaido University (~1993–2004), and Tohoku University (~2004–2018).

Kiyozo Kazama studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held faculty posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Klaus Bruhn studied at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and Ludwig Alsdorf. An Indologist who founded Berliner Indologische Studien, he was professor of Indian philology and Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1994.
